title: Counting bound on descriptions of size-at-most-s circuits
mathematical_statement: Fix n>=1 and s>=0. In the model of topologically ordered circuits with n designated input wires, at most s gates each chosen from AND, OR, NOT with fan-in at most two, and one designated output wire, the number M of circuit descriptions is at most (s+1)(n+s)(3(n+s)^2)^s. The explicit incidence-vector candidate representation therefore has an update circuit of size at most M+1, hence at most (s+1)(n+s)(3(n+s)^2)^s+1. This does not establish a polynomial update bound or a lower bound for other representations.
assumptions: ["circuits have n designated inputs, at most s gates of types AND, OR, NOT with fan-in at most two, one output wire"]

title: Explicit candidate-filter update of size O(K(s+n)+n)
mathematical_statement: Fix n and a finite list C_1,...,C_K of Boolean circuits, each with n inputs and at most s fan-in-two gates. Stream the truth table in binary input order, maintaining an n-bit index i and K live bits a_j, where a_j=1 exactly when C_j agrees with every streamed bit so far. On receipt of bit b, the exact update can be implemented by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with O(K(s+n)+n) gates: each e_j = a_j AND [C_j(i)=b] and the index increments modulo 2^n. The bound does not give a polynomial-in-s update for the full circuit list nor a bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.

title: Corrected exhaustive one-pass EXT decision bound
mathematical_statement: Fix n>=1 and s>=0. Consider Boolean circuits on n inputs with at most s fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates, constants 0 and 1, and one designated output. There is a deterministic one-pass algorithm deciding whether each streamed truth-table prefix extends to the truth table of a circuit in this class. It stores at most D=(s+1)(n+s+2)(3(n+s+2)^2)^s candidate bits, uses O(Ds+n+s) elementary operations per streamed bit and O(D+n+s) working bits. For circuits with exactly j gates the number of descriptions is at most (n+j+2)(3(n+j+2)^2)^j, and summing over 0<=j<=s gives D. A live bit remains iff the prefix has a completion in the class. The bound is exponential, gives no polynomial update bound, and gives no lower bound for arbitrary representations.

title: Explicit-family EXT update with n+M state bits
mathematical_statement: Let F=(C_1,...,C_M) be a fixed list of Boolean circuits on n inputs, each with at most s fan-in-two gates, with streamed bits the truth table of length 2^n in binary input order. There is a deterministic exact EXT-prefix update representation using n+M state bits and at most O(n+M(s+1)) fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates per update. The state stores the next index i in n bits and a candidate mask a in M bits; on next bit b, evaluate each C_j at i, set a'_j=a_j AND [C_j(i)=b], and increment i modulo 2^n. After k updates a_j=1 exactly when C_j agrees with all k streamed bits. M may be exponential, so this does not bound the implicit family of all size-s circuits by poly(s,n).

title: Explicit-family streaming update with live-candidate vector
mathematical_statement: Let F=(C_1,...,C_d) be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits on n input bits, each with at most s fan-in-two gates. title: Logarithmic-tail completion circuit for an existential projection
mathematical_statement: Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of h gates, constants and wiring free. No MCSP lower bound is claimed.

title: Fibre identity for joint owner intersections
mathematical_statement: Owners i with S_i subset of X x Z and fibres A_i^z = {x : (x,z) in S_i}. For nonempty T, the intersection over i in T of S_i is empty iff for every z in Z the intersection over i in T of A_i^z is empty. Consequently the joint MUS clutter is the minimal elements of the intersection over z of the fibre up-sets.

title: Minimal state count of exact streaming recognizers equals distinct residuals per layer
mathematical_statement: Let L be any language of fixed-length words {0,1}^N recognized exactly by a deterministic left-to-right streaming machine. For each depth t and prefix p in {0,1}^t let R_L(p)={u in {0,1}^(N-t): pu in L}. (1) Any such machine has at least |{R_L(p): p in {0,1}^t}| distinct states after t symbols. (2) The layered machine whose depth-t states are the distinct sets R_L(p), with transition R_L(p) --b--> R_L(pb), recognizes L exactly. (3) Hence the minimum number of states at layer t equals the number of distinct residuals R_L(p) at that depth. Scope: all N>=0, all Boolean languages L in {0,1}^N, one bit per transition, fixed known depth; no uniformity, transition gate complexity or MCSP simulation is claimed.

title: Nondeterministic verification bound for EXT prefixes
mathematical_statement: Fix n,s and an explicit binary encoding of fan-in-two Boolean circuits with at most s gates, each gate record using O(log(n+s)) bits, output wire specified in the description. Let N=2^n. For each t in {0,...,N}, EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 for p in {0,1}^t iff there exists a valid description d of at most L=O(s log(n+s)) bits whose circuit C_d agrees with p on the first t inputs in the fixed truth-table order. Then EXT_{n,s}(p) is in NP with witness length at most L+O(1) and deterministic verification time O(t(s+n)+L) in a standard gate-list encoding. This is a nondeterministic upper bound and certificate cost only; no deterministic transition algorithm, no compression, no hardness lower bound.

title: Unit pinning selects MUSs containing the pinned constraint
mathematical_statement: Let F be a finite constraint family, u the unit constraint x_j = c, and F' obtained from F minus {u} by substituting x_j = c. Then MUS(F') = {M minus {u} : M in MUS(F), u in M}.

Let F be a finite constraint family, let u be the unit constraint x_j=c, and let F' be obtained from F\{u} by substituting x_j=c. Then MUS(F') = {M\{u}: M in MUS(F), u in M}. Proof: for every S subset F\{u}, S is inconsistent in F' iff S union {u} is inconsistent in F. If S is minimally inconsistent in F', every proper T subset S is consistent in F'; moreover S is consistent in F, since otherwise S union {u} would not be minimal. title: Residual-language quotient gives minimum layer width
mathematical_statement: Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. For t<=N and prefix p in {0,1}^t define R_p={u in {0,1}^(N-t): pu in F}. (2) The residual sets at each layer form a deterministic layered automaton with transitions R -> {v in {0,1}^(N-t-1): bv in R} on input bit b, initial state F, and acceptance at layer N iff the empty string lies in R. (3) Hence the minimum number of states at layer t equals the number of distinct residual sets {R_p: |p|=t}. Scope: all finite binary languages F and layered automata reading exactly N bits; no bound on transition circuit cost or on simulation through arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

title: Right-residual characterization of minimal state count

title: Fixed-depth residual distinguishability for finite word families
mathematical_statement: Let L be a finite set of binary words of common length N, and let p and q be words of the same length t. Define R_p={z in {0,1}^(N-t): pz in L} and R_q analogously. In every deterministic automaton accepting exactly L, if R_p != R_q then the states reached after p and q are distinct. Consequently the number of states reached by length-t prefixes is at least the number of distinct residual sets R_p at that depth. This applies to EXT for any finite family of equal-length truth tables; it is an information-state lower bound only.

For each position t define the hardwired mask m_t in {0,1}^K by (m_t)_j=E_j[t]. Given candidate bitset x in {0,1}^K and next streamed bit b, define x'_j=x_j AND (b iff (m_t)_j). This is correct for filtering the candidates consistent with the extended prefix and has a fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit of at most K+1 gates for each fixed t. The masks across all t encode the candidate truth tables, so no polynomial-in-(s,n) update bound follows when K is large. The record states that Q-156fa9c912 remains open.

title: Residual-quotient width bound for finite families
mathematical_statement: Let F be a finite family of K Boolean strings of common length N. At depth t, 0<=t<=N, partition all length-t prefixes by equality of their residual sets R(p)={z: pz in F}. The number of equivalence classes is at most min(2^t,K)+1. Nonempty residual classes are witnessed by length-t prefixes of members of F, giving at most min(2^t,K) nonempty classes, plus at most one class for empty residuals. The bound is a width bound in terms of |F| and does not bound transition circuit cost from a compact representation of F.

title: Separate projection of shared-auxiliary constraints does not commute with intersection
mathematical_statement: Let X = {0,1}, Z = {0,1}, E1 = {(x,z) : x = z} and E2 = {(x,z) : x = 1 - z}. Then proj_X(E1) = proj_X(E2) = X, but proj_X(E1 intersect E2) is empty. Replacing constraints on shared variables Z by their separate projections can turn an inconsistent conjunction into a satisfiable one.

title: One-hot transition gate bound for explicit prefix automata
